requested.title: Unvalidated `__mochiBlob` / `__mochiBlobRef` sentinel turns cached data into an arbitrary-file-read handle
Superseded blob files are never reclaimed for a continuously-refreshed key, so the entry folder grows without bound
Blob-folder deletion races a concurrent `setItem`, persisting an entry whose pointer dangles
`markStale` read-modify-write can silently revert a concurrently written value
JSON object keys are emitted unescaped into HTML, giving DOM XSS at the debug bar's {@html} sinks
Remote binary fetched with no integrity verification and written into the committed source tree
WebView constructed outside the try/finally that stops the dev server — a construction failure orphans or wedges it
Dev server stdout/stderr are piped but never read — swallows boot diagnostics and can stall the server on pipe backpressure
freePort() has a TOCTOU window: the probe releases the port before the dev server claims it

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: I verified every mechanical claim in the current source. `getItem` (L309-326) calls `this.decodeBlobs(parsed.__mochiValue)` unconditionally — there is no `offloadBinary` gate on the decode side, confirmed both by reading the method and by the existing test at cache-storage-file.test.ts:529 ('entries written with offloadBinary on still read as BlobRefs after the flag is dropped'), which makes flag-independent decoding an intentional design property. `isBlobPointer` (L54-56) requires only that the object carry a *string* `__mochiBlob` property — `bytes` is never validated and `readBlobRef` doesn't even read it — and `decodeBlobs` (L582) builds `path: join(this.directory, value.__mochiBlob)` with no `resolve`/`startsWith` containment check, so `'../../../../etc/passwd'` normalizes out of the cache dir. `readBlobRef` (L45-47) then does `Bun.file(ref.path).arrayBuffer()` with no check of its own. The encode-side mirror is real too: `encodeBlobs` leaves a plain object with a `__mochiBlob` key untouched (it falls through to the generic object branch at L567-572) and converts any `{__mochiBlobRef:true, path}` shape into `relative(this.directory, value.path)` (L560-562), so an absolute path round-trips as a `../`-laden pointer. `isBlobRef`/`readBlobRef` are public exports (`index.ts:27`) and `packages/docs/145-cache.md:160` documents exactly the vulnerable idiom ('Resolve one with `readBlobRef(ref)`, and narrow a value with `isBlobRef(value)`') while the Callout promises that any JSON-serializable value round-trips and never reserves the `__mochi*` keys. Concrete attack: an app caches an attacker-shaped structured document (upstream API response, webhook body, user-controlled JSON column) through `MochiCache({storage: new FileStorage(...)})`; the attacker plants `{"__mochiBlob":"../../../../../../etc/passwd"}` in a nested field; the next read promotes it to a `BlobRef` and the app's documented `isBlobRef(x) ? readBlobRef(x) : x` branch discloses the file. I confirmed the finding's own honest caveat: no in-tree consumer is reachable — `MemoryStorage` never encodes/decodes at all, `ImageCache` stores a fixed `StoredImage`/`StoredPlaceholder` shape whose only binary field comes from `fetchSource`/`runPipeline` as a real `Uint8Array`, and `packages/site/src/lib/ci.ts`'s dev-only `FileStorage` holds app-mapped GitHub data. So this is a latent arbitrary-file-read in a published library primitive rather than a live hole in the deployed sites — MEDIUM is the right rating, and the repo's own 'patterns to flag' list already treats joining an untrusted name onto an output directory without rejecting `..` as in scope.

Confirmed on all three reclamation paths. `setItem` (L336-349) only `mkdir`s and writes blobs it doesn't already find on disk — it never enumerates or prunes `<keyHash>/`. Sweep pass 1 (L443-473) keys off the *owning JSON's* mtime, and `setItem` writes a fresh temp (`open(path,'w')`) and renames it over `<hash>.json` (L352-355), so every revalidation resets that mtime; a key refreshed at least once per `maxAge` can therefore never age out, and the folder `rm` at L463-464 is reached only via that aged-out branch. Sweep pass 2 (L477-494) explicitly only touches folders whose owning JSON is *absent*, which by construction excludes a live entry. The L545-549 comment's claim that superseded blobs are 'reclaimed with the whole entry folder by removeItem or the sweep' is thus false for a continuously-refreshed key, and the test at cache-storage-file.test.ts:412-428 confirms retention is deliberate ('The superseded blob is left on disk (reclaimed with the folder later)'). The ImageCache scenario checks out numerically: `imageCache.ts:166` builds `FileStorage({maxAge: maxTimeToLive, purgeInterval: 0, offloadBinary: true})`, `image/config.ts:103-104` defaults `timeToStale` to 14_400_000 (4h) and `timeToEvict` to 86_400_000 (24h), and `sweeper.ts` drives `cache.sweep(Date.now())` into exactly that pass-1 mtime check. A source whose upstream bytes change (CMS re-upload at a stable URL, rotating banner) regenerates roughly every 4h under steady traffic; each distinct byte generation adds a new content-addressed blob under the same original and variant key hashes, and the refreshing JSON mtime keeps those folders out of pass 1 indefinitely. Identical bytes do dedupe (same digest → the `exists()` skip at L341), and `markStale` re-persisting a read-back `BlobRef` pushes nothing onto `blobs`, so neither of those inflates the folder — the leak is strictly one blob per changed generation, which is what the finding says. The companion `.tmp` claim is also correct: blob temps are written as `<keyHash>/<digest>.bin.<uuid>.tmp` *inside* the folder (L344) while pass 1's `readdir` is top-level only (no `recursive`), so crash debris there is invisible to both passes while the entry lives.

Distinct from F2 (growth vs. corruption) and structurally confirmed. `setItem` is a two-phase commit — blobs renamed in first (L339-348), JSON renamed last (L352-355) — and nothing serializes it against `removeItem`'s unconditional `rm(join(directory, hash), {recursive, force})` (L369) or sweep pass 1's identical `rm` (L464). Both are `async` with multiple awaits, so the interleaving is reachable in a single-threaded event loop: writer renames the blob in, deleter unlinks the (possibly absent) JSON and recursively removes the folder, writer's JSON rename then lands on an untouched top-level path and succeeds. The window is not instantaneous — it spans `fsyncDir(blobDir)` plus a full `writeFileDurable` (open/write/fsync/close) on the JSON temp, i.e. real fsyncs. Importantly, `removeItem` `rm`s the folder even when no JSON existed, so a *first* population racing an unconditional `invalidateOriginal(src, true)` → `cache.delete(origKey)` hits it too. I verified the guard placement: `cache.ts:368` checks inflight identity and generation *synchronously* and then awaits `storage.setItem`, so a `delete` arriving during that await cannot stop the write — and `set()`'s own docstring (L217-218) concedes exactly this gap, while commit 9b7c65c2's message states the fix 'deliberately does not cover a fetch whose own write was already issued to the backend'. The consequence chain is confirmed: `decodeBlobs` never stats the target, so `getItem` hands back a `BlobRef` to a missing file; `ImageCache.toBytes` → `readBlobRef` throws ENOENT, which is not an `ImageError`, so `imageEndpoint.ts`'s catch returns `textResponse(500, 'Image processing failed')`. Because the corrupted JSON carries a fresh envelope `createdAt`, `MochiCache.lookup` reports 'fresh' and never revalidates, so every subsequent request re-reads the same dangling pointer and 500s for up to `minTimeToStale` (4h at image defaults) rather than transiently. Reachable from ordinary traffic, not just the janitor: `getVariant` deletes a present variant key when the original is gone/expired (imageCache.ts:240-242) and `cascadeSource` deletes variants and placeholders (L388-416), either of which can land while a background revalidation (`cache.ts:162`) is mid-`setItem` on the same key. The L545-549 comment reasons only about rewrites and does not cover deletion, which is the gap.

The structural defect is unambiguous: `markStale` reads the entry at L243, derives `next` from the value it captured, and writes it back at L258 with no re-validation in between; `supersedeRuns` at L240 only clears the in-flight slot and bumps the generation, which stops a run that has not yet reached its sync guard but cannot stop `set()` (which consults no generation and writes unconditionally at L224) nor a run already inside `storage.setItem`. Any write landing in that gap is therefore reverted to the older value *and* backdated, so the stored value moves backwards a generation even though the L236 contract only promises the timestamp can 'only move staler'. Commit 9b7c65c2 fixed the mirror-image race (an unregistered fetch clobbering an invalidator) and its message explicitly scopes out 'a fetch whose own write was already issued to the backend', so this direction is genuinely unaddressed. Where I disagree with the finding is its reachability claim: `ImageCache.getVariant` does call `markStale` on a hot path (imageCache.ts:248-250), but I traced it and it cannot lose a regen's write, because markStale only fires when `existing.status === 'fresh'` and a key with an in-flight run is by definition stale/expired/absent — in which case markStale's own early return at L253-255 (or the null check at L248) makes it a no-op. ImageCache's key spaces are also disjoint: `set` is used only on `phKey` (setPlaceholder, L468), while `markStale` only ever targets `varKey`/`origKey`, and placeholders are never `fetch`ed. So there is no in-tree trigger. The concrete trigger is at the public API: `markStale` is documented (packages/docs/145-cache.md:96,101) alongside the guidance at cache.ts:207-218 to prefer `set()` for an atomic replace, and an app issuing `set(k, v)` concurrently with `markStale(k)` on a fresh entry silently loses the `set`. With `FileStorage` + `offloadBinary` the reverted pointer still resolves (superseded blobs are intentionally retained, per F2), so the regression is invisible rather than erroring. Narrow and self-healing on the next revalidation, which is why BUG rather than anything higher — but the unguarded read-modify-write is real.

I confirmed both defects at the byte level. `od -c` on line 36 shows literally `str.replace(/&/g, '&').replace(//g, '>')` — each character replaced by itself, a faithful carry-over of upstream 1.0.4's broken escape pass, so there is no global escaping at all (the unused `entityMap` at L11-19 shows the intent). The per-match branch then escapes only *values*: at L40-47 a match starting with `"` and ending with `:` is a key and gets nothing but `color = colors.keyColor`, while only the value branch at L45 calls `escapeHtml`; `match` is interpolated raw at L51. `JSON.stringify` does not escape `<`, `>` or `&`, and the regex's `[^\\"]` class happily spans ``, so that key survives L31/L37 intact and is emitted inside a ``. I traced the full client-side chain for the exploitable sink, `IslandRow.svelte`: for server islands, `serverIslandCrypto.ts:38` records `JSON.stringify(devalParse(propsJson), jsonSafeReplacer, 2)`; `Mochi.ts:175`'s `jsonForHtml` escapes `<` to `\u003c` only for the HTML-parsing layer, so after JS parsing the string holds a real `<`, and `JSON.parse(recorded)` at IslandRow.svelte:40 restores the raw key before `formatHighlight(rest)` at L42 is rendered through `{@html}` at L115. The code description is accurate — `fetchDango()` (L67-75) checks only `response.ok`, performs no digest/content-type/magic-byte/size validation, writes the bytes straight to `src/og/assets/dango.png`, and `DANGO_SOURCE` (L65) pins a mutable git *tag* rather than a commit SHA; `cards.ts:33` does load the committed file through `@napi-rs/canvas`'s native `loadImage()` and memoises it for the process lifetime. But I could not construct an attack reachable by any in-scope attacker, and the mitigating chain is specific and verifiable. First, the script is not automated anywhere: grepping every `package.json` and workflow file shows no reference to it — `packages/site/package.json` has only build/start/dev/typecheck/test/clean, and nothing in `.github/workflows` invokes it. Its own header says 'Re-run only when the card's design changes', and `git log` shows `dango.png` written exactly once (6f616f94). Second, nothing attacker-influenced feeds the fetch: the URL is a hardcoded constant with no parameterization, so there is no request path, env var, or user input that can redirect it. Third, the downloaded bytes cannot reach production without a human `git commit` — and a maintainer re-running the bake script is doing so precisely to eyeball the regenerated card, so substituted artwork is the visible output of the step, not a silent side effect. Fourth, the only 'attacker' in the chain is a compromise of (or force-moved tag in) Google's `googlefonts/noto-emoji` org, which is an out-of-scope precondition rather than an exploitable condition; and even granting it, impact beyond a defaced OG card additionally requires a Skia decoder 0-day. That is materially weaker than the two supply-chain items the project's own threat model names (`create-mochi`'s tarball download and `update-skill`'s fetch), both of which run on end users' machines as part of published tooling. The recommendation itself — pin by commit SHA, assert a hardcoded SHA-256, or drop the fetch and verify the in-tree asset — is sound hardening and worth doing, but as a vulnerability finding at MEDIUM this does not survive: there is no exploitable path, which the finding effectively concedes ('a hardening gap rather than a live exploit').

Confirmed by reading the control flow: `startDevServer()` spawns `bun run dev` at L111-117 and `stopServer` is assigned at L201, but the only teardown is the `finally` at L269-272 attached to the `try` that opens at L223 — while `new Bun.WebView({...})` is evaluated at L212-221, before that `try`. Any throw from the constructor therefore skips `stopServer?.()` entirely while the dev server is already running. The constructor does throw in exactly this script's target environments: Bun's WebView docs state 'If Bun finds none, the constructor throws' when no Chrome/Chromium/Edge/Brave is on PATH or in a standard location, and that is the non-darwin path `CHROME_BACKEND` at L19 exists to serve (CI, Docker, the repo's dev container); the same page also documents throws for `backend: "webkit"` off macOS, for construction inside a Worker, and for `headless: false`. The dimension sub-claim is weaker than stated — the docs give `width`/`height` as 'Range 1-16384' for the constructor without explicitly saying it throws out of range (only `resize()` is phrased as a hard requirement) — but `toNumber()` at L77-87 really does validate only `Number.isFinite`, so `--w -5`, `--w 0` and `--w 1e6` all reach the constructor unclamped, and `frameSize()` in src/shot/registry.ts clamps the server side only, never the WebView argument. The consequence is confirmed from Bun's own spawn docs (/docs/runtime/child-process): 'The parent bun process does not terminate until all child processes have exited. Use proc.unref() to detach' — so the outcome is either a permanent hang holding a live dev server, or (if the unhandled rejection hard-exits) an orphaned `bun run dev` tree still bound to its port, accumulating one more on every failed invocation. Compounding it, the thrown error is maximally uninformative because the server's stderr was piped and discarded (F8). The fix is straightforward: move the construction inside the `try`, or register teardown immediately after `startDevServer()` resolves.

The first half is certain and verified exhaustively: `Bun.spawn` is called with `stdout: 'pipe'` and `stderr: 'pipe'` (L114-115), which per Bun's docs expose `ReadableStream`s on the `Subprocess`, and `proc` is referenced only at L121 (`.exitCode`), L127 and L134 (`.kill()`) — nothing in the file ever reads either stream, and `startDevServer` returns only `{base, stop}`, so no closure retains them either. That means both failure paths throw the least useful error available while holding the explanation unread: L121-123 raises `Dev server exited with code N before it started answering.` and L135 raises the 120s timeout, in each case discarding the stderr that would name the port collision, Svelte compile error, or missing env var. For this package that is a real operator cost, since `packages/site`'s dev entry is a full Mochi boot with compilation. The second half — pipe backpressure stalling the dev server — is plausible but not something I can establish from source alone: Bun's docs do not specify whether an unconsumed `pipe` stream is drained into an internal buffer or left in the OS pipe, so whether the ~64KB kernel buffer fills and blocks the writer depends on Bun internals I'd have to run to confirm (and the task is static-analysis only). The scenario is nonetheless well-motivated for the `--keep-open` path specifically: `stopServer` stays undefined there (L200-202), so the server runs indefinitely with `consoleLogger()` emitting a line per request and no reader attached, and per Bun's spawn docs the parent cannot exit while that child lives. I'm scoring this true-positive on the certain half; the recommendation (drain and include the captured stderr in both error messages, or just use `'inherit'`) resolves both halves at once.

The race is structurally present exactly as described. `freePort()` (L101-106) binds `Bun.serve({port: 0})`, reads `probe.port`, calls `probe.stop(true)` and returns the number; the port is only actually claimed later, in a different process, when `Bun.spawn(['bun','run','dev'])` at L111-117 boots and binds it. I confirmed the child really does consume that number rather than ignoring it: the spawn passes `PORT`/`MOCHI_PORT`, `packages/site/package.json`'s `dev` script is `NODE_ENV=development bun src/index.ts`, and `src/index.ts:114` reads `Number(process.env.PORT) || 3333`. So between the probe's release and the child's bind, anything on the machine can take the port — including a second concurrent `shoot.ts`, which this script makes trivial to run. The secondary claim also checks out against Bun's docs: `stop(closeActiveConnections?: boolean): Promise<void>` and 'The returned promise resolves once every connection has closed', yet L104 discards that promise, so the probe's listener may still be closing when the child attempts the bind. The diagnostic impact compounds with F8: the child dies with EADDRINUSE, its stderr is discarded, and the operator sees either a bare `Dev server exited with code N` or a full 120-second wait, with nothing pointing at a port race. The window is narrow in practice (the kernel generally doesn't hand back a just-released ephemeral port immediately), which matches BUG severity rather than anything higher — but `await probe.stop(true)` at minimum, and ideally letting the server pick its own port and parsing it from a drained stdout, are the right fixes.
